headline: On the hottest day of the summer, walkers on 72% of Milton Keynes' footpaths faced very strong heat stress.
deck: That is a feels-like temperature of 38 °C or more, for at least an hour.
sources: Environment Agency lidar flown in the winters of 2019–20 and 2020–21 gives the shape of the area; a custom deep-learning model sorts its points into ground, buildings, trees and water. SOLWEIG (Lindberg et al. 2008) follows the sun over them hour by hour on 13 August 2026 and, with the Met Office's 2 km UKV air temperature, humidity and wind, gives the feels-like temperature (UTCI) on each 1 m square. Footpaths are from OpenStreetMap, bus stops from NaPTAN; places built since the flight are greyed. New trees are placed as TreePlanter does (Wallenberg et al. 2022). Urban means the census areas the ONS classes as urban (2021). From a UTCI of 38 °C (very strong heat stress), a walker's core temperature starts to rise within half an hour (Błażejczyk et al. 2013).

urban.headline: 650 trees and 34 shelters would spare people waiting at all 1,145 bus stops from very strong heat stress.
urban.deck: As it was, 442 of them reached 38 °C.

stops.label: Shade at bus stops
stops.headline: 729 trees and 45 shelters would spare people waiting at all 1,283 bus stops from very strong heat stress.
stops.deck: As it was, 492 of them reached 38 °C.
stops.note: 729 new trees, the fewest that shade every stop in each hour it would reach 38 °C, and a shelter at the 45 stops no tree can shade. Each is 9.7 m tall, the median of the trees beside paths and stops now.

trees.name: trees

urban.headline: 10% more trees would cut the footpaths where walkers face very strong heat stress, from 70% to 43%.
urban.deck: Every bus stop would stay below 38 °C too, with a shelter at each of the 26 that no tree can shade.

trees.label: 10% more trees
trees.headline: 10% more trees would cut the footpaths where walkers face very strong heat stress, from 72% to 45%.
trees.deck: Every bus stop would stay below 38 °C too, with a shelter at each of the 37 that no tree can shade.
trees.note: 91,716 new trees, one for every 10 standing now: first by the bus stops, then where they shade the most sunlit footpaths in the hottest hours. Each is 9.7 m tall, the median of the trees beside paths and stops now.
